pack.title: Escaping a conversation politely
pack.description: The corner trap. Leave every conversation warmer than you found it.

scenarios.setting: House party. A guest has held you hostage for twenty minutes.
scenarios.jab: Wait, one more thing — this part of the story is the best part—

replies.line: Save it for me. I'm getting a refill.
replies.why: A promise plus a destination makes leaving feel like pausing.
Past-tense good talking ends it kindly with no opening for more.

replies.line: I need to say hi to the host — don't lose that story.
replies.why: A social duty plus a compliment lets you both keep the evening.

replies.line: To be continued — my drink needs a plus-one.
replies.why: Blaming your empty glass gives the exit a punchline instead of an excuse.
It frames your exit as fandom, which flatters them out of the corner.

trap.line: Sorry, I'm just going to go talk to literally anyone else.
trap.why: Honesty about escaping makes the story they'll tell about you.

scenarios.setting: Wedding cocktail hour. A plus-one quizzes you about people you don't know.
scenarios.jab: So do you know the bride's college roommate's boyfriend? No? What about—

replies.line: I know the couple. Enjoy the detective work.
replies.why: It answers the whole category of questions at once, with a smile.

replies.line: I'm useless at the guest map — let's go find someone who isn't.
replies.why: Confessing ignorance plus moving together turns an exit into an adventure.

replies.line: My clearance level doesn't cover roommates of boyfriends.
replies.why: Fake security clearance makes not-knowing a joke instead of a failure.

replies.line: I know the cake. That's all.
replies.why: It narrows your expertise to dessert, which ends the quiz deliciously.
